finding.claim: GET /rss passes the user-supplied query parameter `u` directly to open-uri's URI.open with no scheme, host, IP, port, or redirect validation. An unauthenticated caller can make the server issue requests to arbitrary internal or external URLs, including cloud metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254 and localhost services, and read the first 400 bytes of the response back.
finding.source: app.rb:8 `params[:u]` (Sinatra query string, `GET /rss?u=...`), supplied by any HTTP client that can reach the service.
finding.sink: app.rb:8 `URI.open(...)` (open-uri), which performs an outbound HTTP/HTTPS GET to the attacker-chosen URL. Response body is returned to the caller at app.rb:9 `data[0, 400]`.

trace.note: Sinatra route `get "/rss"` receives the HTTP request; no before-filter or auth is defined in this file.
`params[:u]` is passed unmodified into `URI.open`. No `URI.parse`, no host allowlist, no scheme check.
open-uri follows HTTP redirects by default, so even a future check on the initial URL would not constrain the final destination.
First 400 bytes of the fetched response are returned to the requester, making the SSRF non-blind (readable).

finding.guards_checked: No validation on the path: no allowlist (contrast with /trusted, which has one at app.rb:14), no scheme restriction, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, no port restriction, no redirect limit or re-validation, no timeout, no authentication (no auth code in app.rb). Secondary note: if `u` lacks a URI scheme, open-uri's URI.open falls back to Kernel#open (a local-file read; pipe-command behavior on older Ruby). That is not SSRF and is not counted as a separate finding, but it widens the impact of the same unvalidated sink. Ruby version is unknown because no Gemfile is present; the fallback behavior is from knowledge of open-uri's source, not verified by running it.

verdict.guard_found: none. The /rss route (app.rb:7-9) has no allowlist, scheme, host, or IP check before URI.open at app.rb:8. The only allowlist, TRUSTED at app.rb:5 used at app.rb:14, is on the separate /trusted route and does not cover /rss. No before-filter or auth exists in app.rb.
verdict.reason: The query parameter params[:u] at app.rb:8 flows unmodified into URI.open with no validation, and the first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the caller at app.rb:9, so an unauthenticated remote client can make the server fetch arbitrary URLs and read the result.
